scope: source-first intake of named Mine ore and gem nodes; no V0 floor placement or card promotion

source_facts.fact: Copper Nodes yield Copper Ore and may occur on any Mines floor; Iron Nodes yield Iron Ore and concentrate on floors 40–79; Gold Nodes yield Gold Ore and occur from floor 80. Amethyst and Topaz Nodes can occur throughout the Mines and yield their respective gems. These source-game floors are not LVC Depth numbers.
Ordinary Mines rocks can drop Geodes, whose opening is a separate process. A named Geode Node is not assumed to occupy an LVC Mine source slot.

source_facts.source: Stardew Valley: The Board Game rulebook — Explore the Mine, p. 17
source_facts.fact: Explore the Mine compresses mining into one action with possible Stone, Ore, Geode, Staircase and other results; its Mine Level card determines available Ore and Geodes. This is evidence for family-level compression, not for copying its dice or result table.

issues.note: CG-20 fixes the first floor at 2 Rock + 2 normal Ore Rock + 2 Dense Ore Rock and every later floor at 2 Rock + 4 Dense Ore Rock. Adding or replacing a source changes the owner-approved floor composition; no candidate receives a slot here. A later depth band with its own source distribution is a proposal, not a decision.
Current Ore Rock produces generic Ore, and three generic Ore guarantee the Copper Pickaxe upgrade. Named Copper/Iron/Gold Ore outputs must not silently replace that item or alter the upgrade path.
The source game's 40/80 floor bands, multiple pickaxe hits and variable ore yields have no direct LVC Depth, AP or quantity mapping. Resolve once for a selected Mine expansion, not node by node.

selection_review.reason: The named nodes share a candidate Break-to-Item-to-spent loop, but cannot be placed into CG-20's fixed six-source floors or substituted for generic Ore without changing progression. Their source-game depth and quantity data are recorded as references only.
